title: Bardeen alternatives, with checked prices | 50agents
description: Bardeen now sells lead finding. For browser automation, try Gumloop, Lindy, the Zapier Agents extension, Power Automate RPA or 50agents. Prices checked.
answer: Bardeen now sells one thing, finding and enriching sales leads, so if you used it to automate work in your browser, look at Gumloop, Lindy or the Zapier Agents Chrome extension.

For old desktop apps, Power Automate's desktop flows are the RPA option; for scheduled jobs on websites with no app, such as checking competitors' prices, 50agents builds a browser agent from plain words.
ask: Track my leads and follow up
lede: Bardeen's site today is about prospecting: an AI web scraper that finds leads, qualifies them and adds contact details, billed per row.

entries.suits: Recurring jobs on public websites, such as checking competitors' pricing pages every morning. A browser agent runs on a schedule and leaves a report.
entries.limit: It is not built to scrape thousands of rows, and it cannot log in to a site for you without your OK.

entries.suits: Teams whose browser work needs logins: the AI agent browses with saved logins, and you can review or take over its browser.
entries.price: No free plan. Pro: $37 a month (20,000 credits)
entries.limit: No free plan: Pro is $37 a month for 20,000 credits after a trial that needs a card.

entries.suits: People who want an assistant for email and calendar that can also drive a browser for them.
entries.price: $50 in credits for 7 days. Team: from $29.99 a month per active user
entries.limit: Browser use is on Pro and up, not the entry plan.

entries.suits: People who liked Bardeen's "do something with this page" moment. The Zapier Agents Chrome extension works on the page you have open.
entries.price: Free: 100 tasks a month. Professional: $19.99 a month billed yearly (750 tasks)
entries.limit: Zapier Agents are billed in activities, apart from Zap tasks, so you watch two meters.

entries.suits: Windows teams automating desktop apps and websites with RPA, where there is no API at all.
entries.price: Free for cloud flows with standard connectors. Premium: $15.00 per user a month, paid yearly
entries.limit: Attended RPA needs the $15 per user Premium licence; unattended bots are $150 each a month, paid yearly.

us: Your browser work is a few public pages on a schedule, and you want a report, not a spreadsheet of thousands of rows.
The site has an app in the catalog, so an automation can do the job without a browser at all.
You want the job described in plain words, not recorded click by click.
them: You use it for prospecting: finding leads on the web, qualifying them and enriching contacts. That is what Bardeen is built for now.
You want ready-made scrapers and enrichment, with free CSV downloads.
Your volume fits the credits: Basic's 100 credits enrich about 33 leads.

move.title: Download your data first
move.body: Bardeen lets you download results as CSV at no cost, or send them to Google Sheets, Airtable or Notion. Do that before you cancel.

move.title: Name the websites and the schedule
move.body: For each job, write the sites it visits, what it reads, and when it should run. That is the whole brief for a browser agent.

move.title: Prefer an app over a browser
move.body: If the site has an app in the catalog (HubSpot or Shopify, say), connect the app instead. It is faster and does not break when the page changes.

move.title: Check the first runs by hand
move.body: Open the pages the browser agent visited and compare them with its report for a few days before you rely on it.

faqs.q: Is Bardeen still a browser automation tool?
faqs.a: Its current site describes a sales tool: an AI web scraper that finds, qualifies and enriches leads. We found no mention of general browser automation on its current pages.
Every account keeps 100 free credits. Basic is $10 a month for 100 credits a month; Premium is $50 a month, or $480 a year for 12,000 credits.

faqs.q: What is the best Bardeen alternative for scraping?
faqs.a: For scraping behind logins, Gumloop, with its credential vault. For a few pages on a schedule, 50agents or Lindy. For Windows desktop apps, Power Automate.
